name: Felt
label: Creation Records
lede: Lawrence decided Felt would make ten albums and ten singles in ten years, went through guitarists and bassists on the way, and ended the band on schedule in 1989.

eras.title: A single called 'Index'
eras.text: Lawrence (born Lawrence Hayward) made the first Felt record alone. The band he built around it came from his village outside Birmingham, and the guitarist he found there gave Felt its early sound.

years.h: Lawrence pays for 'Index' and Sounds makes it single of the week
years.p: The self-released solo single gets the nod from Sounds writer Dave McCullough. The name Felt comes from the way [[Tom Verlaine|b54065f0-61b3-4f6f-ba4a-ce15564fbd59]] leans on one word in [[Television|490bde43-5edb-4a93-b3b3-7a0465fd8909]]'s 'Marquee Moon'.

years.h: Maurice Deebank tunes Lawrence's guitar in three seconds
years.p: Lawrence brings in [[Maurice Deebank|1201e15c-3d8a-48a5-9e3c-d4275b7ed1fc]], a classically trained guitarist from Water Orton, and Nick Gilbert on drums. Deebank becomes his co-writer.
years.xp:
"One day I got him round and he tuned my guitar in three seconds," Lawrence remembered. He has also said he wanted to "ride on his back to the top."

Deebank's ornate playing defines the early records. [[Johnny Marr|ff621094-2a76-401f-8398-b75b5fd2be24]] has named him as an influence.

years.h: Gary Ainge takes the drums and stays to the end
years.p: Gilbert moves to bass, Tony Race drums briefly, then [[Gary Ainge|326a8cec-a352-4812-8fe8-f26efa713f56]] arrives. He's the only member besides Lawrence on all ten albums. Felt signs to [[Cherry Red|47df8f8d-46a7-489a-97ac-ce9dccd3b424]].

eras.title: Cherry Red, and a guitarist who comes and goes
eras.text: Four albums on Cherry Red, a guitarist who left for a solo record and came back, and an indie No. 1 with a Cocteau Twin singing on it. Then Deebank left for good.

years.h: Crumbling the Antiseptic Beauty, and a spot on Pillows & Prayers
years.p: The first album. 'My Face Is on Fire' goes on Cherry Red's best-selling sampler Pillows & Prayers.
years.xp: Nick Gilbert quit after the draining sessions and Mick Lloyd came in on bass. Deebank took a sabbatical to make the instrumental Inner Thought Zone, out on Cherry Red in 1984.

years.h: Two albums in one year, the second one pop
years.p: Deebank is back for The Splendour of Fear and The Strange Idols Pattern and Other Short Stories, which pushes the band toward pop.

years.cap: Martin Duffy (left) with Felt in Birmingham
years.h: An 18-year-old Martin Duffy answers Lawrence's call
years.p: Lawrence finds the keyboard player through a contact at the Virgin Megastore in Birmingham. Marco Thomas takes the bass.

years.cap: Felt playing live on Catalan TV's Estoc de Pop, c. 1985
years.src: Wikipedia: Ignite the Seven Cannons · Wikipedia: Felt (band)
years.h: Elizabeth Fraser sings on 'Primitive Painters', an indie No. 1
years.p: The [[Cocteau Twins|000fc734-b7e1-4a01-92d1-f544261b43f5]] singer's voice is all over the band's most successful single, which tops the UK independent chart.

q: He kind of ruined some of my best songs.
years.h: Robin Guthrie produces, and Deebank's time is up
years.p: The only Felt album with both Deebank and Duffy. Deebank leaves for good after it.
years.xp: Lawrence never liked the mix by [[Robin Guthrie|47d7b25e-585b-4c97-b98b-411b21a53379]], though he allowed that Guthrie would probably agree "now he's a lot more experienced!" The 2018 reissue remixed six tracks.

eras.title: Creation, and the organ takes over
eras.text: On Alan McGee's Creation Records, Duffy's organ moved to the middle of the sound. Felt put out records at a rate that kept Lawrence's ten-year count on track, including two with no singing at all.

years.h: The first Creation album has no vocals
years.p: Let the Snakes Crinkle Their Heads to Death is Felt's first all-instrumental record. [[Phil King|88ccf29e-2c88-4cb5-8e2b-9d575371b34f]] joins on bass.

years.src: Wikipedia: Forever Breathes the Lonely Word
years.h: NME later calls it "the first truly classic Creation album"
years.p: Recorded with John A. Rivers at Woodbine Street in Leamington Spa, it's Felt's first album with no instrumentals, built around Duffy's Hammond.

years.h: Poem of the River keeps it low and close
years.p: A quiet, intimate record. Phil King leaves the same year and later turns up in [[Lush|697801d1-68b2-4413-a7e4-0ef507d21cc1]].

years.cap: Felt in Birmingham, 1988, Martin Duffy on the right
years.h: Pop songs on one side, Duffy's piano on the other
years.p: The Pictorial Jackson Review splits the record down the middle.

years.h: Lawrence directs a jazz record and plays nothing on it
years.p: Duffy and Ainge write and play Train Above the City on vibes, piano and drums. Lawrence runs the sessions and names the tracks.
years.xp: Melody Maker's review said it "bears no obvious relationship to anything else they've done."

eras.title: Ten and ten, on time
eras.text: The last album went to Cherry Red's él label, with a Primal Scream guitarist on bass. Then Lawrence explained the plan.

years.src: Wikipedia: Me and a Monkey on the Moon
years.h: Robert Young of Primal Scream plays bass on the last album
years.p: [[Adrian Borland|7ba9565d-dc78-4616-b1c2-9c6191d3b5cc]] of the Sound produces Me and a Monkey on the Moon in Eastbourne in ten days in August. [[Rose McDowall|aad85c3e-48d8-43e9-876e-49bafba607b2]] and [[Pete Astor|e9cb7de9-0508-4e3a-b370-bb23c4b1578d]] sing backup.
years.xp: It's lusher than anything before it, with B.J. Cole on pedal steel and Lawrence writing more personally. Sounds called it "perhaps their finest album yet."

years.cap: Felt in Birmingham, with Martin Duffy on the right
years.h: Ten albums, ten singles, ten years, and Felt stops
years.p: Lawrence says the plan was always to quit at ten of each. After a short tour, the band splits.

years.big: "The reason Felt didn't make it is because John Peel didn't like us"
years.h: Lawrence has his own explanation for why Felt didn't break
years.p: Lawrence, looking back on ten albums and an indie No. 1 that never crossed over.

eras.title: Denim, Mozart and a marble bust
eras.text: Duffy went to Primal Scream for three decades. Lawrence kept going under new names, lost his flat, and became the subject of a documentary and a sculpture.

years.h: Back in Denim swaps Felt for '70s glam and bubblegum
years.p: Lawrence's new band Denim makes two albums; a third is shelved. [[Go-Kart Mozart|aebf6275-de8e-4d12-bb79-088b8ffb48bc]] follows from 1999, later renamed Mozart Estate.

years.cap: Lawrence around the time of Lawrence of Belgravia, c. 2011
years.h: Lawrence of Belgravia premieres in London
years.p: Paul Kelly's documentary debuts at the London Film Festival. It follows the man who was evicted from his Belgravia flat in 2005 and spent time homeless and in hostels.

years.h: Martin Duffy, Felt's organist and Primal Scream's, dies at 55
years.p: He joined [[Primal Scream|55704c38-224f-4b75-b29f-d43653f8bc9a]] full time after Felt and stayed more than 30 years. He died in Brighton of a brain injury from a fall at home.
years.xp: Two Felt bassists had died before him: Mick Lloyd in 2016 and Mick Bund in 2017.

years.cap: Lawrence in Fitzrovia at the Fitzrovia Chapel, London, 2024
years.h: Lawrence gets a pink marble bust at the Fitzrovia Chapel
years.p: The Portuguese marble bust goes on show in London. Q had named him Maverick of the Year in 2018, when Cherry Red reissued all ten Felt albums with new mixes he oversaw.
